conventions.planet_maps: Equirectangular (plate carree). Image left edge = longitude -180, centre = 0, right edge = +180 (east-positive); top row = latitude +90, bottom = -90. Body-fixed frame for shading: +X = (lat 0, lon 0), +Y = (lat 0, lon +90 E), +Z = north pole. Lookup: u = 0.5 + atan2(y, x) / (2 pi), v = 0.5 + asin(z / r) / pi (v measured from the bottom, as Blender does).
conventions.planet_maps_blender_recipe: Material: Texture Coordinate.Object -> Mapping (type Vector, Scale 1, -1, 1) -> Environment Texture (Equirectangular). Verified in Blender 4.5 Cycles: object +X samples u=0.50, +Y samples u=0.75 (lon +90 E), -X samples the u=0/1 seam, lat +30 samples v=0.667. Do NOT use the Image Texture node's SPHERE projection with Object coordinates (it samples the wrong place).
conventions.sky_maps: milkyway_8k.jpg is in ICRS/J2000 equatorial coordinates: image centre = RA 0h, Dec 0; RA increases to the LEFT (u = 0.5 - RA/360, wrapping); top row = Dec +90. stars.csv uses the same RA/Dec.
conventions.sky_blender_recipe: World: Environment Texture with the image and no rotation puts RA 0h/Dec 0 on world +X, RA 6h on world +Y, the north celestial pole on world +Z (Cycles maps u = 0.5 - atan2(y, x)/(2 pi); verified). If the scene's XY plane is the ecliptic (+X = vernal equinox, +Z = ecliptic north pole), feed Texture Coordinate.Generated through a Mapping node (type Vector, Rotation X = +23.4393 deg); verified that a Vector-type Mapping rotation applies d' = Rx(theta) d. Star directions from stars.csv in the same ecliptic frame: d_ecl = Rx(-23.4393 deg) d_eq, with d_eq = (cos dec cos ra, cos dec sin ra, sin dec).
conventions.srgb_textures: All colour JPEGs are sRGB-encoded; load as sRGB in Blender to get linear values. Height, mask and cloud-coverage maps are data: load as Non-Color.
conventions.radiometric_units: render/lib.py convention: Cycles Sun strength = irradiance in W/m^2 with the 1 AU solar constant 1361 W/m^2. Equivalent photometric conversion for anything referenced to V magnitudes or cd/m^2: divide by about 93 lm/W (solar luminous efficacy), since 1361 W/m^2 <-> 1.27e5 lux.

files.content: Mercury surface albedo (Lambert-equivalent), sRGB-encoded linear reflectance
files.frame: Mercury planetocentric, east-positive longitude, lon 0 at image centre
files.scale: Decoded linear luminance has an area-weighted mean of 0.080; 2nd/50th/98th percentiles (|lat|<60) are 0.051 / 0.077 / 0.118. Mean linear colour R:G:B = 1.066 : 0.992 : 0.889 (slightly red-sloped grey). Multiply in the shader to change the albedo level; see CREDITS.md for how 0.08 was chosen.

files.content: Mercury elevation, uint16 lossless JPEG 2000 (reversible 5/3 wavelet; bit-exact; Blender 4.5 reads it exactly)
files.scale: height_m = -6000 + 1.0 * stored_value; relative to the 2,439,400 m reference sphere. Blender normalised value n = stored/65535, so height_m = -6000 + 65535 * n. Displacement node: Midlevel = 0.0915541 (6000/65535), Scale = 65535 m expressed in scene units. Data range -5380 .. +4485 m (stored 620 .. 10485).

files.content: Mercury elevation, 16-bit greyscale PNG, area-averaged from the 8k grid
files.scale: Same encoding as mercury_height_8k.jp2: height_m = -6000 + stored_value (1 m steps).

files.content: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation, July 2004 (cloud-free, no shaded relief, no bathymetry)
files.frame: geographic WGS84 lon/lat, lon -180 left edge
files.scale: Display-referred true colour (sRGB), not calibrated albedo

files.content: NASA Black Marble 2016, lights only (greyscale), area-averaged from 13500x6750
files.scale: Relative brightness; the source JPEG's tone curve is undocumented. Starting point: decode as sRGB and map 1.0 to about 1e-3 W/m^2/sr (bright urban core, VIIRS DNB about 100 nW/cm^2/sr), emission colour about 3000-4000 K.

files.content: NASA Black Marble 2016 lights only (greyscale), 500 m tile C1 cropped to lon 20-65 E, lat 5-50 N and box-averaged to 1 km
files.frame: geographic, left edge lon 20 E, top row lat 50 N
files.scale: Same tone encoding as earth_night_lights_8k.jpg but 17 % brighter on average over this region; multiply decoded linear values by 0.855 to match it.

files.content: As above at the tile's full 500 m, cropped to lon 44-58 E, lat 22-38 N
files.frame: geographic, left edge lon 44 E, top row lat 38 N
files.scale: Multiply decoded linear values by 0.855 to match earth_night_lights_8k.jpg.

files.content: NASA Blue Marble cloud composite, greyscale
files.scale: 0 = clear, 255 = opaque cloud; load Non-Color and use as coverage/alpha

files.content: Ocean/sea mask from GEBCO_08 bathymetry (255 = water)
files.scale: Area-averaged, so coasts are fractional. Inland seas such as the Caspian, Black Sea and Baltic count as water; freshwater lakes (Superior, Victoria) and ice shelves count as land.
files.license: Public domain (NASA EO image of GEBCO data)

files.scale: Relative only; the vertical scale is not documented in the source file. Use for bump detail only.
files.license: Public domain (NASA EO image of GEBCO data)

files.content: Moon colour mosaic, NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit (LRO LROC WAC, lroc_color_poles_2k), re-encoded as JPEG
files.frame: selenographic, lon -180 left edge, lon 0 (sub-Earth) at centre, east-positive; top row = lat +90
files.scale: Display-stretched: decoded linear luminance has an area-weighted mean of 0.30. Multiply by 0.40 for a Lambert-equivalent normal albedo with the Moon's mean of 0.12.
files.license: Public domain (NASA SVS / LRO LROC); credit NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio

files.content: Every HYG v4.4 star with V <= 8.00 (Sun excluded), brightest first; columns ra_deg, dec_deg (ICRS J2000, epoch 2000), vmag (Johnson V), bv (B-V)
files.notes: 112 rows (0.3%) had no B-V: 93 were estimated from spectral type and 19 set to 0.65. Point-source irradiance in the repo convention: E = 1361 * 10^(-0.4 * (V + 26.74)) W/m^2 = 2.74e-8 * 10^(-0.4 V) W/m^2.

files.content: Diffuse sky background: NASA SVS Deep Star Maps 2020 'milkyway' layer (Gaia DR2 stars) plus the 'hiptyc' layer with every stars.csv star (V <= 8) masked out, so stars.csv can be drawn as point lights without double counting while Tycho-2 stars with 8 < V < 11.5 stay in the background
files.frame: ICRS equatorial, RA 0h at centre, RA increasing to the left, Dec +90 top (galactic centre at pixel x=6225, y=2706)
files.scale: Pure linear scale + sRGB transfer, no tone curve. Decoded linear d (0..1) -> SVS linear value p = d * 0.126568; only the brightest 0.05% of pixels are clipped. Calibration from SVS star photometry (V 5-8 stars, about +/-30%): p = 1 corresponds to about 0.027 cd/m^2, about 2.9e-4 W/m^2/sr in the repo convention. Background Strength for this image in render/lib.py units: about 3.7e-5 (= 0.126568 * 2.9e-4). Check: the galactic-centre 10x10 deg mean comes out at about 19.4 V mag/arcsec^2 and the all-sky mean at about 21.9.
files.license: NASA SVS (public domain in the US); credit NASA/GSFC SVS and ESA/Gaia/DPAC

files.frame: local east/north metres from 43.7535 N, 110.7195 W; column 0 = 14 km west, row 0 = 13 km north (teton_dem.json)
